newsitem.title: CHILE: Pay rebels to free hostages, says ex-Peru premier.
newsitem.headline: Pay rebels to free hostages, says ex-Peru premier.

text.p: Peru should pay leftist guerrillas to free the 400 hostages they are holding hostage in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, former Peruvian prime minister Alfonso de los Heros said on Friday.

"Giving them money and taking them to a neutral country could be a way out that avoids freeing prisoners and executing hostages," said de los Heros, who served in President Alberto Fujimori's government.
"If they avoid an exchange of prisoners and hostages, (the rebels) may get other conditions in their favour," he told evening newspaper La Segunda.
Armed rebels from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement stormed the residence three days ago, capturing ministers, ambassadors and businessmen who were attending a diplomatic reception.
The Peruvian government has so far refused to negotiate with the Marxist guerrillas, who are threatening to kill their hostages if their demands for the freeing of jailed comrades are not met.
Red Cross officials have warned that conditions within the overcrowded building were worsening with the captives sleeping on the floor in crumpled suits and having to wait in line for scarce toilets.
